facts.conditions: Recommended VCC=3..3.6 V and free-air TA=-40..85 C. Voltages except differential bus values reference network ground. Receiver thresholds are over recommended conditions; section 8.6 cites Table 1 (V(Rs)=1.2 V), typical values at 25 C/VCC=3.3 V. Common mode is the average of CANH/CANL, not an independent allowance for arbitrary ground offset, noise and driver bias added together. Between threshold bounds no new deterministic state is asserted. Individual, differential and common-mode conditions must be considered together; Table 1 test cases do not expand section 8.3 into a general pin-voltage permission.

facts.conditions: Section 8.1 stress ratings over operating free-air temperature unless noted; all nondifferential voltages reference network ground. Transient numbers require Figure 24 pulse setup through 100 ohm, not a continuous common-mode range or arbitrary surge/fault survival. Functional operation outside recommended conditions is not implied; prolonged stress may impair reliability.

facts.conditions: Arrays correspond in order to the three RS settings. Section 8.9 over recommended conditions; Figure 26 measures D to R with 60 ohm +/-1% across CANH/CANL, R load 15 pF +/-20%, RS resistors +/-5%, D pulses rise/fall <=6 ns at 125 kHz and 50% duty, thresholds at 50%. These are transceiver loop bounds, not a total controller/cable/sample-point budget. Do not promote typical columns to guaranteed limits or transfer SN65HVD232 behavior.

facts.conditions: SN65HVD230 wake with RS, over recommended conditions; typical at 25 C/VCC=3.3 V. Figure 25: D=0 V, 60 ohm bus load, R pull-up 10 kohm and CL=15 pF; RS generator 150 kHz/50% duty, rise/fall <6 ns, 50 ohm source. Timing is falling RS crossing 1.5 V to R crossing 1.3 V, not a full controller interrupt-to-transmit deadline. Existing 230 standby receiver stays active; controller must drive RS low to reactivate the driver after sensing traffic. Do not use SN65HVD231 receiver-off sleep or its 3/5 us row.

facts.conditions: Section 11.2.1.2 uses typical values and a rule of thumb; both cable directions are counted in (535-70)/(2*5).
